transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Well, um, I guess... it's just that things have gotten really, really out of hand lately. I work down at the dry cleaners, pressing shirts and dealing with all those heavy machines, and it gets so incredibly hot and stressful in there all day. And... well, what brings me in is that I keep making myself throw up after I eat. 

It’s like I can't stop myself anymore. I mean, sometimes I even do it right there in the tiny employee bathroom at work, which is just so awful and embarrassing because the walls are paper thin and I'm always terrified my supervisor is going to walk by and hear me. But I just get this overwhelming urge and I have to do it. Or, if I somehow manage to hold off while I'm on the clock, I do it the exact second I get home. Literally right when I walk through the door to my apartment, before I even take my work shoes off or put my bag down, I head straight for the bathroom. 

I just hate it. I really, really hate that I do it, and I feel so ashamed of myself, but... at the exact same time, it’s like it has started feeling like the absolute only way I can calm down. My brain just races and the stress from the day builds up so much, and getting rid of the food is the only thing that makes my chest stop feeling so tight, you know? It just gives me this weird sense of relief for a minute, so I keep doing it, and I just don't know how to break the cycle anymore.
Do you find yourself overly concerned about your weight or the way your body looks, especially before or after you eat?

Oh, constantly. It's... it's honestly all I think about, all day long. You know, at the dry cleaners, we have these big plate glass windows up at the front where the customers come in, and there's all this glass around the counter, too. And I can be having a perfectly fine day, you know? Like, I'm getting all the heavy coats done, the machines are running smooth, I'm dealing with the customers just fine... I can be doing really, really good at the shop. But then I'll just happen to walk past the front, and I'll catch my reflection in the glass. And if my stomach or my hips look big to me in that split second... it just ruins absolutely everything. 

I instantly feel like a complete and utter failure. It just washes over me. It doesn't matter how hard I've worked or how much I got done that shift, because all I can focus on is how huge I look. Our work uniforms are these stiff, awful shirts, and I'll just start pulling at the fabric, obsessing over every little bulge, wondering if everyone else sees how big my stomach is. I'll just stand there staring at my reflection, picking apart my waist and my hips, and I just feel so deeply disgusted with myself. 

And then that feeling, that heavy, horrible feeling of being fat and worthless, it just follows me around for the rest of the day. It's like my whole worth as a person is entirely based on whether my stomach looks flat in that one piece of glass. And especially after I eat... if I even have a bite of something on my break, I'm right back at the glass, or checking the mirror in that tiny bathroom, pulling my shirt tight to see if my stomach sticks out more than it did an hour ago. It's just exhausting. It really, really is, but my mind just won't let it go.
Can you describe what typically happens before you feel the urge to vomit? Do you find yourself eating large amounts of food in a short period of time, even when you’re not hungry?

Yeah, um... yeah, that's exactly it. It’s... well, let me try to explain how it usually goes, because it’s hard to even make sense of it myself. Usually, it starts when the stress just peaks, you know? Like, I'm not even physically hungry at all. My stomach isn't growling or anything like that. But I get this sort of... tunnel vision. 

Like, if I'm walking home from the cleaners after a really exhausting shift, I'll stop at the little corner store down the block from my apartment. And it's like my brain just switches off and I'm on complete autopilot. I just start grabbing things off the shelves. When it happens, I mean... I can go through a full bag of chips, like the really big family-sized ones, and a bunch of packaged pastries from the corner store, plus whatever random leftovers I have sitting around in the fridge at home, and wash it all down with these huge sweet drinks. 

And I do all of that in just one sitting. I just sit there and eat it all so fast, practically shoving it in. I don't even really taste it half the time, I'm just chewing and swallowing. Before I even really notice how much is gone, the wrappers are just sitting there completely empty all around me. It's like I'm desperately trying to shove down all the anxiety and the exhaustion from standing on my feet all day pressing shirts, just trying to numb my brain out. But then the food is gone, and my stomach is stretched so tight it physically hurts, and I look at the mess and realize what I just did. That's when this horrible, suffocating panic sets in, and the guilt is just so heavy, and that's exactly when I get that overwhelming urge that I just have to get rid of it.
How often do you make yourself vomit after these episodes of overeating?

Well, gosh, if I really sit down and track it... it’s been going on for months now. Like, a really, really long time. I’d say that most weeks, almost every single week, honestly, I have at least a couple of these episodes where I just completely lose control and eat way, way more than I ever meant to. 

And then... well, then the panic hits and I just have to try and undo it. Throwing up is the main thing, like I said, especially right when I get home. But it's not even just that, you know? Because sometimes, if I feel like throwing up wasn't enough, or if the guilt is just eating me alive the next morning, I'll try to undo it in other ways, too. I'll just completely fast. I'll go the whole entire next day just drinking black coffee and water, my stomach totally empty and cramping, telling myself I'm fixing what I did the night before. 

Or... or I'll try to exercise it all off. I'll just pace around my apartment for hours or do these frantic, exhausting workouts in my tiny living room until my legs feel like absolute jelly and I can barely even stand up to go press shirts the next day. It's just this constant, exhausting math in my head, you know? For months now, at least a couple times a week, it's just this exact same nightmare cycle of eating too much and then desperately trying to erase it by throwing up, or starving, or exercising myself into the ground. It's like I'm working two full-time jobs—one at the dry cleaners, and one just trying to manage all this... this mess. I just can't seem to stop trying to balance the scales.

Do you feel like these episodes of overeating—where you feel like you've completely lost control—are something that happens over and over again, and do they always lead to you making yourself vomit or doing something else to try to get rid of the calories?

Yes. Yes, it’s exactly like that, just... over and over again. It’s this endless loop that I’m completely trapped in. And the part about losing control... that’s the absolute scariest part of all of this, honestly. Because once I start, once I open that first bag of chips or whatever it is I brought home from the store, it feels like my hands just keep reaching for food even while I am literally telling myself to stop. 

I’ll be sitting there on my couch, usually still wearing my uniform, smelling like industrial starch and steam, and my brain is just screaming, 'Stop, put it down, you’re going to regret this, look at what you’re doing!' But my hands just keep moving. They just keep grabbing and unwrapping and shoving it in. It’s... it's almost like an out-of-body experience, you know? Like I am watching myself do it from across the room and I absolutely cannot make myself quit. I'm just a spectator watching myself ruin everything, totally helpless to stop my own arms and mouth. 

And because of that... because I watch myself do this and can't stop it, the panic that comes right after is just so unbearable. So, yes, it always, always leads to me having to fix it. Every single time. I can't ever just let the food stay inside me after an episode like that. The guilt is just too heavy, it feels like I'm going to crawl out of my skin. So the second the wrappers are empty, I'm rushing to the bathroom to make myself sick, or I'm immediately planning out how I'm not going to eat a single crumb the entire next day at the cleaners, or I start doing those frantic workouts I told you about. 

I just have to get rid of it. I have to. Because if I don't, I'll just be sitting there with all that food inside me and the horrifying memory of not being able to control my own hands. It’s just so humiliating, you know? To feel like you don't even have a say over your own actions... so I just keep repeating the exact same nightmare and desperately trying to erase it, week after week.
